scenes.heading: Trigonometric ratios review
scenes.sub: Three ratios that unlock every right-angled triangle
scenes.say: Heights of trees, slopes of ramps, flight paths of planes. Every trigonometry problem starts with the same three ratios. Let’s make sure they are rock solid.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Your left is your friend’s right: it depends where you stand
scenes.science: Opposite and adjacent depend on which angle you stand at
scenes.breaks: The hypotenuse never changes: it is always the longest side, across from the right angle.
scenes.say: If you face a friend, your left hand is on their right. Left and right depend on where you stand. Opposite and adjacent are the same: they depend on which angle you stand at. But the hypotenuse never changes. It is always across from the right angle.

scenes.heading: Name the sides from θ
notes: Hypotenuse: across from the right angle
scenes.say: First the triangle, with its right angle. Then the angle theta in the corner. The hypotenuse is across from the right angle. The opposite side is across from theta. And the adjacent side is the one that touches theta but is not the hypotenuse.

scenes.heading: SOH CAH TOA
scenes.equation: sin = O/H, cos = A/H, tan = O/A
scenes.say: Now the three ratios. Sine theta is opposite over hypotenuse. Cosine theta is adjacent over hypotenuse. Tangent theta is opposite over adjacent. Remember it as soh, cah, toa.

scenes.heading: Write the three ratios
scenes.question: Opposite 5 cm, adjacent 12 cm, hypotenuse 13 cm. Write sin θ, cos θ, tan θ.
scenes.say: Here the hypotenuse is thirteen, the opposite side is five and the adjacent side is twelve. So sine theta is five over thirteen, cosine theta is twelve over thirteen, and tangent theta is five over twelve.
scenes.caption: H = 13, O = 5, A = 12. So sin θ = 5/13, cos θ = 12/13, tan θ = 5/12.

scenes.heading: Exact values from a half-equilateral
scenes.say: Cut an equilateral triangle of side two in half. You get sides one, root three and two, with angles of thirty and sixty degrees. So sine thirty is one half, cosine thirty is root three over two, and tangent sixty is root three.
scenes.caption: Sides 1, √3 and 2, angles 30° and 60°. sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 60° = √3.

scenes.heading: An exact-value calculation
scenes.question: Find the exact value of tan 60° × cos 30°.
scenes.say: Find tan sixty times cos thirty, exactly. Tan sixty is root three. Cos thirty is root three over two. Root three times root three is three, so the answer is three halves.

points: Label sides from θ: H, O, A
sin and cos are always less than 1
scenes.say: Quick recap. Label the sides from theta. Use soh cah toa. Sine and cosine are always less than one. Get exact values from the two special triangles, and use degree mode for everything else. Now try the practice questions!
